intro.patientBody: This is where you check in on your treatment goals — usually once a week. Each check-in takes a couple of minutes, and your clinic sees your answers so they can adjust your care. When something is due, you'll see it right here on this screen.
intro.physiotherapistBody: Unlock a patient with the visit code they show you. You can then record how their treatment goals are progressing, suggest new goals, and flag muscles for the physician to consider at the next injection visit.
intro.clinicianBody: Unlock a patient with their visit code to review goals, record a treatment, and see how the patient and their therapist have rated progress. Patient and therapist suggestions appear on the patient's page for you to act on.
intro.clinicianHowBody: You unlock one patient at a time with the visit code they bring. The session stays open while you work and times out when you are done, so the next patient starts clean. This app is a shared space for goals and progress — it is not your clinical record, and it does not diagnose, dose, or replace your usual notes.
intro.physiotherapistHowBody: You unlock one patient at a time with their visit code. While the session is open you record progress on their goals, suggest new goals or muscles for the physician to consider, and can record assistive devices in the patient's information. Your own clinical notes stay in your usual record system.
intro.comfortBody: Set the text size and light or dark mode so the app is easy on your eyes. You can change these anytime from the menu in the top corner.
intro.comfortWhereHint: You can change these anytime from the menu in the top corner.
intro.graphBody: Each goal has a graph. The coloured bands show how the week compares to what was expected — they are descriptive, not a pass or fail. The y-axis is the outcome level, not a raw score.
intro.graphTryHint: Tap any dot to see that week's rating and any note. The sage line is the patient's own rating; the amber line is the therapist's assessment. A grey ring marks a week that was skipped.
intro.graphSampleGoal: Hold a cup of tea steadily
intro.actionsBodyClinician: From a patient's page these open inline: patient suggestions to review, therapist input, the cross-cycle history, and the EHR export.
intro.actionsBodyTherapist: From a patient's page you can report progress, suggest goals or muscles for the physician, and record assistive devices in the patient's information.
intro.recordBodyClinician: Record what you injected — date, product, dilution, guidance, and the muscles with their doses. The total is entered after the muscle list. If there was a previous treatment, you can copy it into the form with one tap and adjust from there. This becomes the patient's treatment record for the cycle.
intro.recordBodyTherapist: Rate how each goal is progressing and add a short note for the physician to see at the next visit. The patient's own ratings stay separate from yours.
intro.checkinBody: Once a week you rate each goal on a simple 0–10 scale, with a couple of words if you like. It takes a minute, and your care team sees your answers so they can adjust your treatment.
intro.detailsBody: This helps your care team and, in anonymous form, supports research. Both are optional — you can skip and add them later in your profile.

help.patientHomeBody: This is where your weekly check-ins appear. When one is due, you'll see it here — tap it to rate how your goals are going. It only takes a minute, and your care team sees your answers so they can adjust your treatment.
help.checkinBody: Rate each goal on a 0–10 scale for how things feel this week. You can add a few words if you like — your care team reads these. There are no right or wrong answers; just answer honestly so the picture stays accurate.
help.clinicianPatientBody: This is your home base for an unlocked patient. The graphs show how each goal has progressed; the buttons open patient suggestions, therapist input, the cross-cycle history, and the EHR export. Record a treatment from here, and end the session when you step away.
help.treatmentBody: Enter the session details — date, product, dilution, guidance — then add each muscle with its dose. The total goes in below the muscle list, once you've added them all. If the patient had a previous treatment, use Copy last treatment into the form on the Last treatment card to fill everything from last time, then adjust — it's usually the fastest start. Save when done; this becomes the cycle's treatment record.
help.historyBody: These charts show trends across all of this patient's treatment cycles — total dose, goal outcomes, benefit duration, and re-treatment timing. The coloured bands are descriptive (how a result compares to expected), not a pass or fail. It needs at least two cycles to show a trend.
help.newGoalBody: Use this for a goal the patient told you in clinic. Write it in their own words, add your clinical phrasing, then set the 0–10 question they'll answer each week and how their answers map to outcome levels. The goal still belongs to the patient — you're recording it for them.
help.suggestionBody: A patient has suggested a goal. Read it in their words, then approve it as-is, edit and approve, or set it aside to discuss. Approving opens the rating setup — the 0–10 question and outcome levels — so the goal becomes part of their weekly check-ins.
help.physioPatientBody: This is your home base for an unlocked patient. The graphs show how each goal is progressing — your assessments and the patient's own ratings. From here you can report progress, suggest goals or muscles for the physician, and record assistive devices in the patient's information.
help.physioProgressBody: Rate how each goal is progressing and add a short note for the physician to see at the next visit. Your assessment is kept separate from the patient's own weekly ratings, so both points of view stay visible on the graph.

newGoal.title: Record a goal for this patient
newGoal.intro: Use this for a goal the patient told you about in clinic. Write it in the patient’s own words — it becomes one of their active goals straight away.
newGoal.goalPlaceholder: e.g. I want to be able to hold a cup of tea steady.
newGoal.ratingSectionIntro: The patient rates this goal 0–10 each week. You set the question they see and how their answer maps to a GAS level.
newGoal.nrsQuestionPlaceholder: e.g. On a scale of 0-10, how steady is your hand when holding a cup?
newGoal.directionHelp: What ‘higher’ means on the 0–10 scale for this goal.
newGoal.gasLevelsHelp: Optionally describe what each level looks like for this goal, in one sentence each. The patient reads these and picks the level that matches — there is no 0–10 scale. Leave any blank to let the patient rate against the goal text using the level’s general meaning. Describe observable outcomes, with 0 as the expected result of treatment.
newGoal.gasTip: Tip: write the levels so they step up steadily, with no gaps or overlaps between them.
newGoal.levelMuchMorePlaceholder: e.g. Holds a full cup and drinks unaided, no spills.
newGoal.levelMorePlaceholder: e.g. Holds a half-full cup steadily for a few seconds.
newGoal.levelExpectedPlaceholder: e.g. Holds a light cup briefly with some effort.
newGoal.levelLessPlaceholder: e.g. Can grip the cup but not lift it without spilling.
newGoal.levelMuchLessPlaceholder: e.g. Cannot grip the cup at all.
